items.text: Rule 3: adding arrows
Extra structure on a group $G$: arrows between constructions, e.g. $G^{\mathrm{ab}}\to G\times G$; $G^3\to G^4$; $k[G]\to k[G]^{\otimes3}$.
$H$ a small set, $\alpha_1,\alpha_2\colon H\to\operatorname{Ob}R$: for each $h$ an arrow $\alpha_1(h)\to\alpha_2(h)$.
R\ \subset\ R_1=R\,\langle h\colon \alpha_1(h)\to\alpha_2(h)\rangle\ \ (\text{category generated, composites formed})
T'(C)=\{\psi\colon R_1\to C:\ \psi|_R\ \text{a } D\text{-functor}\},\qquad R'=R_1[\Sigma^{-1}]\ \ (\text{via } \widetilde{R_1})
Rule 4: products and limits of theories
Rule D: $(T_\alpha)_{\alpha}$ algebraic ($\alpha$ in a small set) $\Rightarrow$ $\prod T_\alpha$ algebraic; base objects indexed by $\coprod I_\alpha$.
\prod_\alpha T_\alpha\ \ \text{represented by}\ \ \coprod{}^2_\alpha R_\alpha\ \ \text{(2-sum in }\mathbf{Cat}_D)
2-inverse limit of theories $T_\alpha$ (pseudo-functor from a small category): algebraic.
\mathbb L_\alpha T_\alpha\ \ \text{represented by}\ \ \varinjlim{}^2_{\mathbf{Cat}_D}R_\alpha
Example: group $\to$ Lie ring (descending central series), ring $\to$ Lie ring (bracket); fibre product of theories: a group and a ring with an isomorphism of Lie rings.
T_\alpha\to\tau^I\ \ \Longrightarrow\ \ \prod_{\tau^I}T_\alpha\ \text{represented by the 2-amalgamated sum of the } R_\alpha\ \text{over}\ \widetilde I
Definition. A theory is algebraic if obtained by stepwise application of rules A–D (possibly transfinitely).
Each step preserves representability by an $R$ with a small set of $D$-generators; every algebraic structure has a classifying category.
Converse
$R$ small, $I=\operatorname{Ob}R$ generating. Claim: $T_R(C)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_D(R,C)$ is algebraic.
Step 1: $\tau^I$ — the objects $F(x)$, $x\in I$.
Step 2: add the arrows $F(h)\colon F(x)\to F(y)$, $h\in H=\operatorname{Fl}(R)$.
Step 3: axioms “two arrows become equal”: $F(gh)=F(g)F(h)$, $F(\mathrm{id}_x)=\mathrm{id}_{F(x)}$.
Needs kernels in $D'$ or cokernels in $D''$ — or admit axioms of two kinds: arrows becoming isomorphisms, arrows becoming equal.
Step 4: $\Sigma$ = the arrows expressing that $F$ commutes with the limits of type $D'$, $D''$ — to be inverted.
$R$ not small: $D$-generating family $I\to R$, i.e. $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_D(R,C)\to C^I$ faithful for all $C$.
I'=\text{the full subcategory of } R \text{ on } I:\quad \operatorname{Hom}_{I'}(i,j)=\operatorname{Hom}_R(R_i,R_j)
C\mapsto\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(I',C)\ \ \text{algebraic};\qquad I'\to R\ \ \text{canonical functor}
